analyticalQuestion: Does the bivariate support relation s<=2j provide enough charge-degree coupling to repair the inherited large-positive-charge active-tail bound at the preassigned radius r=33/100?
supportedClaim: Every strict-tail input with s>=S and s<=2j obeys j>=max(N+1,ceil(S/2)). At N=80 and S=241 this raises the uniform input-degree floor from 81 to 121. Replacing only the decreasing factor (i+j)/(i+j-1) lowers the all-order large-charge bound at r=33/100 from 1.002872150853994023 to 0.99888144242700740673. The complete active Banach restart and inherited canonical-stretch construction then pass at r=33/100. The next millesimal probe r=331/1000 has improved active-tail bound 1.0038955265828946573 and fails the present sufficient inequality.

chartContract.takeaway: The missing improvement comes from support geometry, not a numerical cancellation: s>=241 forces j>=121, converting the preassigned r=0.330 failure into a strict all-order pass while r=0.331 remains a negative control.
chartContract.dataSufficiency: Twenty-one support rows expose the cone and lattice relation; seven additive bridge rows exactly decompose the total reduction; six proof-gate rows and four boundary rows show the target and adjacent control; 21 finite exact columns test the implementation. The formal sector theorem covers every s>=241 and every admissible j>80 analytically.
